uncertain.item: Aileron direct cables cross above the headliner
uncertain.why: Fig 6-1 labels the LH direct cable (9) on the LH door post but its turnbuckle (13) between B and C, and the RH direct turnbuckle (14) between C and D, with all three cables on cluster C; read as the cable up each post running across the cabin top to the opposite wing. Not stated in text.

uncertain.item: Stations of every pulley, bellcrank and drive pulley
uncertain.why: The manual prints no FS/WS/WL for control-system parts; positions follow the figures' routing order and are fitted to the model (floor, door post, headliner gap, wing, stabilizer). Aft-cabin pulleys (elevator A, rudder C1, trim A1) sit where the model's cabin floor ends (~x 1.8-1.9 m), aft of the figures' apparent FS 90-110.

cable diameters are not printed in D2065-3-13; sizes follow the usual Cessna single-engine practice (1/8 in 7x19 primary flight-control cable, 3/32 in for the control-U chain cables and flap cables, 1/16 in 7x7 trim cable) - estimated

WS not printed; placed at WS 47 (z = +-1.20 m, between the WS 39.00 and 57.12 ribs) aft of the rear spar, where the 8.83 in push-pull rod meets the true-depth flap leading edge; the right motor sits between the drive pulley and the WS 57.12 rib. The placed fastener file uses z = +-1.82 m for the flap push-pull bolt.

The fuel tank fills the bay between the spars inboard of WS 57.12, so aileron and flap cables run aft of the rear spar (x 0.71-0.78) through the trailing-edge rib lightening holes; where a cable passes rib material or within 3 mm of a hole edge a grommet hole / hole enlargement is listed in meta.cutouts_required. Cabin-top cluster C sits on a vertical bolt behind the rear-spar line; the aileron bellcrank is at WS 110 between the WS 100.50 and 118.00 ribs on a rib-to-rib channel.

uncertain.item: Which rudder bar carries which pedals
uncertain.why: Fig 10-2 shows an aft and a forward bar; the left pedals are put on the aft bar. The rudder-bar cable arms point up (a pushed pedal must pull its cable forward) and the cables drop through floor slots to D1.

Fig 5-7 routes them from the rudder-bar arms through firewall boots to the steering arm; here they hang from down-arms so a pushed left pedal pulls the left side of the steering arm (left turn). Steering-arm height on the model's nose strut estimated.

Aileron horn tilt (differential) solved so the bellcrank and cables move symmetrically for FlightGear's -15/+20 deg; bellcrank arms, drum radii, sprocket radius, forward elevator bellcrank arms, rudder-bar arm, trim screw lead and sprocket radii are estimated (not printed).

Linkages follow FlightGear's tables because the visible surfaces do: ailerons are 20 deg TE down / 15 deg TE up in FlightGear vs 20 up / 15 down in Fig 1-1; rudder 13 deg vs 16 deg 10 min; elevator 28/23 as Fig 1-1.

FlightGear moves the yoke a symmetric 0.1 m; with straight (non-differential) rear-bellcrank arms the cable loop stays tight, so column travel here is 0.10 m aft at 28 deg up and 0.084 m forward at 23 deg down.

The model's rudder horn attach points are 0.18 m aft of the hinge line, so the two rudder cables do not pay in and out equally (slack change reported in verification); in the airplane the return springs take it up (para 10-11c).

Screw lead (3/16 in per turn) and sprocket radii estimated (they set the cable travel, about +-0.24 m, and hence the stop-block spacing of Fig 9-2); actuator position in the right stabilizer and the horn under the model's tab estimated. Thread hand chosen to make the wheel sense right (nose down = top forward).
Not built: rudder trim (Fig 10-5) is an option hidden in the FlightGear model; no elevator down-spring appears in Figs 8-1/8-2 for the 172P.

notes.overlay_right_aileron_sign: data/overlay.json drives the right aileron with control 'roll' scale -1; JSBSim (c172p.xml 'Right Aileron Control' takes -roll and maps -20..15 deg onto +1..-1) makes right-aileron-pos-norm follow +roll, so with scale -1 both ailerons go TE down together. Linkages here use +roll; set that animation's scale to 1 for the surfaces to agree.
notes.model_rudder_cable_stubs: The model already has short external rudder-cable stubs (ruddercableleft/right) between the cable ports and the horn; the cables here overlap them.
